title.zh: 卷一百〇三 漢書5: 隱帝本紀下
title.en: Volume 103 Book of Later Jin 5: Emperor Yin Annals 3
title.raw: 卷一百〇三 漢書5: 隱帝本紀下 Volume 103 Book of Later Jin 5: Emperor Yin Annals 3

sentences.zh: 乾祐三年春正月己亥朔，帝不受朝賀。

translations.literal: In spring, on the first day of the first month of the third year of Qianyou (day jihai, new moon), the emperor did not accept court congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: On the new moon of the first month of spring in Qianyou 3, the emperor declined the usual court congratulations.

sentences.zh: 鳳翔行營都部署趙暉奏，前月二十四日，收復鳳翔，逆賊王景崇舉族自燔而死。

translations.literal: Zhao Hui, overall commander of the mobile camp at Fengxiang, memorialized that on the twenty-fourth of the previous month he had recovered Fengxiang; the rebel Wang Jingchong burned himself to death together with his entire clan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Hui, commander of the Fengxiang field headquarters, reported that on the twenty-fourth of the previous month Fengxiang had been retaken and that the rebel Wang Jingchong had burned himself to death along with his whole family.

sentences.zh: 丁未，鳳翔節度使、充西南行營都部署趙暉加兼侍中。

translations.literal: On day dingwei, Zhao Hui, military commissioner of Fengxiang and overall commander of the southwestern field army, was additionally appointed Vice Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei, Zhao Hui—Fengxiang commissioner and commander of the southwestern campaign—was also made Vice Grand Councilor.

sentences.zh: 戊申，密州刺史王萬敢奏，奉詔領兵入海州界，至荻水鎮，俘掠焚蕩，更請益兵。

translations.literal: On day wushen, Wang Wang'an, prefect of Mizhou, memorialized that in obedience to an edict he had led troops into the border of Haizhou; at Dishui town he captured, plundered, and burned, and further requested reinforcements.
translations.idiomatic: On wushen, Mizhou prefect Wang Wang'an reported that under imperial orders he had marched into Haizhou territory, raided and burned Dishui town, and now asked for more troops.

sentences.zh: 詔前沂州刺史郭瓊率禁軍赴之。

translations.literal: An edict ordered Guo Qiong, former prefect of Yizhou, to lead the imperial guard to go to his aid.
translations.idiomatic: The court ordered former Yizhou prefect Guo Qiong to march the palace guard to reinforce him.

sentences.zh: 庚午，前永興軍節度副使安友規除名，流登州沙門島。

translations.literal: On day gengwu, An Yougui, former vice commissioner of the Yongxing army, was stripped of his name and banished to Shamen Island in Dengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On gengwu, An Yougui, former deputy commissioner at Yongxing, was disgraced and exiled to Shamen Island off Dengzhou.

sentences.zh: 先是，友規權知永興軍府事，及趙思綰之奔沖，友規失守城池，至是乃正其罪焉。

translations.literal: Earlier, Yougui had held acting authority over the Yongxing headquarters; when Zhao Siyun fled in alarm, Yougui lost the city. Only now was his crime formally judged.
translations.idiomatic: Yougui had been acting commander at Yongxing; when Zhao Siyun's revolt broke out he lost the city, and only now was he punished for it.

sentences.zh: 癸亥，以前邠州節度使宋彥筠為太子太師致仕。

translations.literal: On day guihai, Song Yanyun, former commissioner of Binzhou, was made Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent and retired.
translations.idiomatic: On guihai, former Binzhou commissioner Song Yanyun was appointed Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent and retired from office.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，分命使臣赴永興、鳳翔、河中，收葬用兵已來所在骸骨。

translations.literal: On day bingyin, separate orders dispatched envoys to Yongxing, Fengxiang, and Hezhong to collect and bury the bones of the dead from all the places where troops had been engaged since the wars began.
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin, the court sent separate envoys to Yongxing, Fengxiang, and Hezhong to gather and bury the war dead scattered since hostilities began.

sentences.zh: 時已有僧聚髑髏二十萬矣。

translations.literal: By then monks had already gathered two hundred thousand skulls.
translations.idiomatic: Monks had already collected two hundred thousand skulls.

sentences.zh: 前沂州刺史郭瓊奏，部署兵士，深入海州賊界。

translations.literal: Guo Qiong, former prefect of Yizhou, memorialized that he had deployed his soldiers deep into the rebel territory of Haizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Former Yizhou prefect Guo Qiong reported that he had pushed his troops deep into Haizhou rebel territory.

sentences.zh: 是月，有狐登明德樓，主者獲之，狐毛長而腹下別有二足。

translations.literal: That month a fox climbed the Mingde Tower; the custodian seized it—the fox's fur was long, and beneath its belly there were two separate feet.
translations.idiomatic: That month a fox climbed Mingde Tower; when attendants caught it, its fur was unusually long and it had a second pair of feet under its belly.

sentences.zh: 二月辛巳，青州奏，郭瓊部署兵士，自海州回至當道。

translations.literal: In the second month, on day xinsi, Qingzhou memorialized that Guo Qiong had deployed his troops and returned from Haizhou to that circuit.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi in the second month, Qingzhou reported that Guo Qiong's detachment had returned from Haizhou to the province.

sentences.zh: 甲申，樞密使郭威巡邊回。

translations.literal: On day jiashen, Guo Wei, Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, returned from inspecting the borders.
translations.idiomatic: On jiashen, Bureau of Military Affairs commissioner Guo Wei came back from his border inspection.

sentences.zh: 丁亥，汝州防禦使劉審交卒。

translations.literal: On day dinghai, Liu Shenjiao, defender of Ruzhou, died.
translations.idiomatic: On dinghai, Ruzhou defender Liu Shenjiao died.

sentences.zh: 乙未，以前安州節度使劉遂凝為左武衛上將軍，以鄜州節度使焦繼勛為右武衛上將軍，以前永興軍節度使趙贊為左驍衛上將軍。

translations.literal: On day yiwei, Liu Suining, former commissioner of Anzhou, was made General of the Left Martial Guard; Jiao Jixun, commissioner of Binzhou, was made General of the Right Martial Guard; Zhao Zan, former commissioner of Yongxing, was made General of the Left Valiant Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: On yiwei, former Anzhou commissioner Liu Suining became Left Martial Guard general; Binzhou commissioner Jiao Jixun became Right Martial Guard general; and former Yongxing commissioner Zhao Zan became Left Valiant Cavalry general.

sentences.zh: 三月己亥，徐州部送所獲淮南都將李暉等三十三人徇於市，給衫帽放還本土。

translations.literal: In the third month, on day jihai, Xuzhou sent up the thirty-three Huainan generals captured, including Li Hui; they were paraded through the market, given shirts and caps, and released to their native places.
translations.idiomatic: On jihai in the third month, Xuzhou forwarded thirty-three captured Huainan officers, including Li Hui; after a public parade they were clothed and sent home.

sentences.zh: 是月，鄴都留守高行周、兗州符彥卿、鄆州慕容彥超、西京留守白文珂、鎮州武行德、安州楊信、潞州常思、府州折從阮皆自鎮來朝，嘉慶節故也。

translations.literal: That month, Gao Xingzhou, regent at Yedu, Fu Yanqing at Yanzhou, Murong Yanchao at Yunzhou, Bai Wenke, regent of the western capital, Wu Xingde at Zhenzhou, Yang Xin at Anzhou, Chang Si at Luzhou, and Zhe Congruan at Fuzhou all came from their posts to court for the Celebration of Good Fortune festival.
translations.idiomatic: That month the regional commanders Gao Xingzhou (Yedu), Fu Yanqing (Yanzhou), Murong Yanchao (Yunzhou), Bai Wenke (western capital), Wu Xingde (Zhenzhou), Yang Xin (Anzhou), Chang Si (Luzhou), and Zhe Congruan (Fuzhou) all arrived at court for the Jiaqing festival.

sentences.zh: 戊午，宴群臣於永福殿，帝初舉樂。

translations.literal: On day wuwu, the emperor feasted the civil and military officials in the Hall of Eternal Felicity; it was the first time he had music performed.
translations.idiomatic: On wuwu the emperor banqueted his officials in Yongfu Hall and, for the first time, had music played.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，鄴都高行周移鎮鄆州，兗州符彥卿移鎮青州，並加邑封。

translations.literal: On day renxu, Gao Xingzhou of Yedu was transferred to Yunzhou and Fu Yanqing of Yanzhou to Qingzhou; both received enlarged fiefs.
translations.idiomatic: On renxu, Gao Xingzhou moved from Yedu to Yunzhou and Fu Yanqing from Yanzhou to Qingzhou, each with an enlarged noble fief.

sentences.zh: 甲子，西京留守白文珂、潞州常思、鎮州武行德並進邑封，鄆州慕容彥超移鎮兗州。

translations.literal: On day jiazi, Bai Wenke, regent of the western capital, Chang Si of Luzhou, and Wu Xingde of Zhenzhou all received enlarged fiefs; Murong Yanchao of Yunzhou was transferred to Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi, western-capital regent Bai Wenke, Luzhou's Chang Si, and Zhenzhou's Wu Xingde all gained enlarged fiefs, while Murong Yanchao moved from Yunzhou to Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 夏四月戊辰朔，邢州薛懷讓移鎮同州，相州郭謹、河陽李暉並進邑封。

translations.literal: In summer, the fourth month, on the first day (day wuchen, new moon), Xue Huairang of Xingzhou was transferred to Tongzhou; Guo Jin of Xiangzhou and Li Hui of Heyang all received enlarged fiefs.
translations.idiomatic: At the summer new moon of the fourth month, Xingzhou's Xue Huairang went to Tongzhou, while Xiangzhou's Guo Jin and Heyang's Li Hui received enlarged fiefs.

sentences.zh: 庚午，府州折從阮移鎮鄧州。

translations.literal: On day gengwu, Zhe Congruan of Fuzhou was transferred to Dengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On gengwu, Fuzhou commissioner Zhe Congruan was reassigned to Dengzhou.

sentences.zh: 辛未，故深州刺史史萬山贈太傅。

translations.literal: On day xinwei, the late prefect of Shenzhou, Shi Wanshan, was posthumously made Grand Mentor.
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei the late Shenzhou prefect Shi Wanshan was posthumously honored as Grand Mentor.

sentences.zh: 先是，契丹入邊，萬山城守，郭威遣索萬進率騎七百屯深州。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the Khitan had entered the borders, Wanshan had held the city; Guo Wei had sent Suo Wanjin to lead seven hundred horsemen to garrison Shenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan had invaded, Wanshan had defended the city while Guo Wei sent Suo Wanjin with seven hundred cavalry to hold Shenzhou.

sentences.zh: 一日，契丹數千騎迫州東門，萬山父子率兵百餘人襲之。

translations.literal: One day several thousand Khitan horsemen pressed the east gate; Wanshan and his son led a little more than a hundred men to strike them.
translations.idiomatic: One day several thousand Khitan riders pressed the east gate; Wanshan and his son led just over a hundred men in a counterattack.

sentences.zh: 契丹偽退十餘里，而伏兵發，萬山血戰，急請救於萬進，萬進勒兵不出，萬山死之，

translations.literal: The Khitan feigned a retreat of more than ten li, then ambush troops rose; Wanshan fought until blood flowed, urgently requesting rescue from Wanjin, but Wanjin held his troops and did not go out, and Wanshan died.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan pretended to withdraw ten-odd li, then sprang an ambush; Wanshan fought on until he was covered in blood and begged Wanjin for help, but Wanjin kept his men in camp and Wanshan was killed.

sentences.zh: 〈（《遼史·世宗紀》：天祿三年殺深州刺史史萬山。）〉

translations.literal: (From the History of Liao, Annals of Emperor Shizong: in the third year of Tianlu the Khitan killed Shenzhou prefect Shi Wanshan.)
translations.idiomatic: (From the History of Liao, Annals of Emperor Shizong: in Tianlu 3 the Khitan killed Shenzhou prefect Shi Wanshan.)

sentences.zh: 契丹亦解去。

translations.literal: The Khitan also withdrew and left.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan then withdrew as well.

sentences.zh: 時論以萬進為罪，故加萬山贈典焉。

translations.literal: Contemporary opinion held Wanjin guilty, and therefore Wanshan was given a posthumous honor.
translations.idiomatic: Public opinion blamed Wanjin, which is why Wanshan received a posthumous enfeoffment.

sentences.zh: 壬申，華州劉詞移鎮邢州，安州楊信移鎮鄜州，貝州王令溫移鎮安州，並加邑封。

translations.literal: On day renshen, Liu Ci of Huazhou was transferred to Xingzhou, Yang Xin of Anzhou to Binzhou, and Wang Lingwen of Beizhou to Anzhou; all received enlarged fiefs.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen, Liu Ci moved from Huazhou to Xingzhou, Yang Xin from Anzhou to Binzhou, and Wang Lingwen from Beizhou to Anzhou, each with an enlarged fief.

sentences.zh: 以鄜州留後王饒為華州節度使，以其來朝故也。

translations.literal: Wang Rao, acting commissioner of Binzhou, was made military commissioner of Huazhou because he had come to court.
translations.idiomatic: Binzhou acting commissioner Wang Rao became Huazhou commissioner in reward for attending court.

sentences.zh: 丁丑，尚食奉御王紹隱除名，流沙門島，坐匿軍營女口也。

translations.literal: On day dingchou, Wang Shaoyin, commissioner of imperial food service, was stripped of his name and banished to Shamen Island for concealing women from military camps.
translations.idiomatic: On dingchou, imperial-food commissioner Wang Shaoyin was disgraced and exiled to Shamen Island for hiding women taken from army camps.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，以宣徽北院使吳虔裕為鄭州防禦使。

translations.literal: On day xinsi, Wu Qianyu, commissioner of the northern bureau of the palace secretariat, was made defender of Zhengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi, northern secretariat commissioner Wu Qianyu was appointed defender of Zhengzhou.

sentences.zh: 時樞密使楊邠上章乞解樞機，帝命中使諭之曰：「樞機之職，舍卿用誰？

translations.literal: At the time Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs Yang Bin submitted a memorial requesting to be relieved of the bureau. The emperor ordered a palace envoy to instruct him, saying: "The bureau post—apart from you, whom should We employ?
translations.idiomatic: Bureau commissioner Yang Bin asked to step down; the emperor sent a palace envoy to say, "Who but you could hold this post?

sentences.zh: 忽有此章，莫有人離間否？」

translations.literal: To have this memorial so suddenly—has someone sown discord?"
translations.idiomatic: This sudden memorial—has someone turned you against us?"

sentences.zh: 虔裕在傍揚言曰：「樞密重地，難以久處，俾後來者叠居，相公辭讓是也。」

translations.literal: Qianyu, standing beside him, spoke out loudly: "The bureau is a weighty post and hard to hold for long; let those who come later take turns in succession—the minister's resignation is right."
translations.idiomatic: Wu Qianyu, standing nearby, called out, "The bureau is too heavy to keep for long; better to let successors take turns—your resignation is the right move."

sentences.zh: 中使還具奏，帝不悅，故有是命。

translations.literal: The envoy returned and reported in full; the emperor was displeased, and therefore there was this appointment.
translations.idiomatic: When the envoy reported this, the emperor was displeased and therefore sent Qianyu away to Zhengzhou.

sentences.zh: 壬午，以樞密使郭威鄴都留守，依前樞密使。

translations.literal: On day renwu, Guo Wei, Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, was made regent at Yedu while retaining the bureau post.
translations.idiomatic: On renwu, bureau commissioner Guo Wei became Yedu regent while keeping his bureau title.

sentences.zh: 詔河北諸州，應兵甲、錢帛、糧草一稟郭威處分。

translations.literal: An edict ordered that all the prefectures north of the Yellow River, as to armor, weapons, cash, silks, and grain, should be entirely at Guo Wei's disposal.
translations.idiomatic: An edict placed all armor, cash, silk, and grain of the Hebei prefectures under Guo Wei's authority.

sentences.zh: 癸未，府州永安軍額宜停，命降為團練州。

translations.literal: On day guimao, the designation of Yong'an army at Fuzhou was to be discontinued and the prefecture reduced to a training command.
translations.idiomatic: On guimao, Fuzhou's Yong'an army designation was abolished and the prefecture downgraded to a training command.

sentences.zh: 戊子，翰林學士承旨、戶部尚書王仁裕罷職，守兵部尚書。

translations.literal: On day wuzi, Wang Renyu, Hanlin academician ex officio and Minister of Revenue, was removed from office and kept on as Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: On wuzi, Hanlin ex officio and revenue minister Wang Renyu was demoted to war minister.

sentences.zh: 左千牛上將軍張瓘卒。

translations.literal: Zhang Guan, General of the Left Palace Guard, died.
translations.idiomatic: Left Palace Guard general Zhang Guan died.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，以西南面水陸轉運使、尚書工部侍郎李穀為陳州刺史。

translations.literal: On day gengyin, Li Gu, transport commissioner for the southwestern land and water routes and Vice Minister of Works, was made prefect of Chenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin, southwestern transport commissioner and vice minister of works Li Gu became Chenzhou prefect.

sentences.zh: 左金吾上將軍致仕馬萬卒。

translations.literal: Ma Wan, retired General of the Left Golden Guard, died.
translations.idiomatic: Retired Left Golden Guard general Ma Wan died.

sentences.zh: 甲午，以前華州節度使安審信為左衛上將軍，以前潞州節度使張從恩為右衛上將軍。

translations.literal: On day jiawu, An Shenxin, former commissioner of Huazhou, was made General of the Left Imperial Guard; Zhang Cong'en, former commissioner of Luzhou, was made General of the Right Imperial Guard.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu, former Huazhou commissioner An Shenxin became Left Imperial Guard general and former Luzhou commissioner Zhang Cong'en Right Imperial Guard general.

sentences.zh: 五月戊戌朔，帝御崇元殿受朝。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, on the first day (day wuxu, new moon), the emperor attended court in the Chongyuan Hall.
translations.idiomatic: At the fifth-month new moon the emperor held audience in Chongyuan Hall.

sentences.zh: 丙午，以皇弟興元節度承使勛為開封尹，加兼中書令，未出閣。

translations.literal: On day bingwu, the emperor's younger brother, Liu Xun, commissioner of Xingyuan and imperial envoy, was made mayor of Kaifeng and additionally Vice Grand Councilor, but had not yet left the inner quarters.
translations.idiomatic: On bingwu the emperor's brother Liu Xun, Xingyuan commissioner, was named Kaifeng mayor and vice grand councilor but had not yet left the palace.

sentences.zh: 甲子，詔：「諸道州府差置散從官，大府五百人，上州三百人，下州二百人，勒本處團集管系，立節級檢校教習，以警備州城。」

translations.literal: On day jiazi, an edict stated: "Each circuit and prefecture shall assign loose retainers: great prefectures five hundred men, upper prefectures three hundred, lower prefectures two hundred; they shall be mustered and registered locally, graded and drilled under inspection, to guard the prefectural city."
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi an edict required: "Every prefecture shall raise local militia—five hundred men for major cities, three hundred for upper, two hundred for lower—register them, train them in ranks, and use them to defend the walls."

sentences.zh: 閏月癸巳，京師大風雨，壞營舍，吹鄭門扉起，十數步而墮，拔大木數十，震死者六七人，水平地尺餘，池隍皆溢。

translations.literal: In the intercalary month, on day guisi, the capital had great wind and rain; barracks were destroyed, the gate leaves of the Zheng Gate were blown up and fell ten-odd paces away, several dozen large trees were uprooted, six or seven people were killed by thunder, water stood a foot or more deep on level ground, and moats all overflowed.
translations.idiomatic: On guisi in the intercalary month a violent storm wrecked barracks, tore the Zheng Gate leaves loose and dropped them ten paces away, uprooted dozens of trees, killed six or seven people with lightning, flooded streets a foot deep, and overflowed every moat.

sentences.zh: 是月，宮中有怪物，投瓦石，擊窗撼扉，人不能制。

translations.literal: That month in the palace there was a creature that threw tiles and stones, struck windows and shook doors, and could not be controlled by people.
translations.idiomatic: That month something in the palace hurled tiles and stones, battered windows and doors, and no one could stop it.

sentences.zh: 六月庚子，以國子祭酒田敏為尚書右丞。

translations.literal: In the sixth month, on day gengzi, Tian Min, libationer of the Directorate of Education, was made Vice Minister of the Right.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi in the sixth month, directorate libationer Tian Min became right vice minister.

sentences.zh: 癸卯，太僕卿致仕謝攀卒，輟視朝一日。

translations.literal: On day guimao, Xie Pan, retired Grand Master of the Stud, died; court audiences were suspended for one day.
translations.idiomatic: On guimao, retired grand master of the stud Xie Pan died and audiences were halted for a day.

sentences.zh: 鄭州奏，河決原武縣界。

translations.literal: Zhengzhou memorialized that the Yellow River had broken its banks at the border of Yuanwu county.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengzhou reported a Yellow River breach on the Yuanwu county line.

sentences.zh: 乙卯，司天臺上言，鎮星逆行，至太微左掖門外，自戊申年八月十二日，入太微西垣，犯上將屏星執法，勾己往來，至己酉年十一月十二日夜，方出左掖門順行，自今年正月十日夜，復逆行入東垣，至左掖門。

translations.literal: On day yimao, the Directorate of Astronomy reported that the planet Saturn had gone retrograde to outside the left side gate of the Supreme Palace Enclosure; from the twelfth day of the eighth month of the wushen year it had entered the western rampart of the Supreme Palace Enclosure, violated the stars Shangjiang, Ping, and Zhifa, and moved back and forth until the night of the twelfth day of the eleventh month of the jiyou year, when it finally came out the left side gate moving direct; from the night of the tenth day of the first month of this year it again went retrograde into the eastern rampart to the left side gate.
translations.idiomatic: On yimao the observatory reported Saturn retrograde outside the Supreme Palace's left gate: since the eighth month of wushen it had entered the western enclosure, brushed Shangjiang, Ping, and Zhifa, shuttled until the eleventh month of jiyou, then exited left moving direct; since the tenth of this year's first month it had retrograded again into the eastern wall to the left gate.

sentences.zh: 秋七月庚午，河陽奏，河漲三丈五尺。

translations.literal: In autumn, the seventh month, on day gengwu, Heyang memorialized that the river had risen three zhang and five chi.
translations.idiomatic: On gengwu in the seventh month Heyang reported the river up thirty-five feet.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，滄州奏，積雨約一丈二尺。

translations.literal: On day yihai, Cangzhou memorialized that accumulated rain measured about one zhang and two chi.
translations.idiomatic: On yihai Cangzhou reported rainfall totaling about twelve feet.

sentences.zh: 安州奏，溝河泛溢，州城內水深七尺。

translations.literal: Anzhou memorialized that the canal had overflowed and water inside the prefectural city was seven chi deep.
translations.idiomatic: Anzhou reported canal flooding seven feet deep inside the city walls.

sentences.zh: 丙子，帝御崇元殿，授皇太后冊，命宰臣蘇逢吉行禮。

translations.literal: On day bingzi, the emperor attended the Chongyuan Hall and invested the empress dowager with her patent; he ordered the chief minister Su Fengji to perform the rite.
translations.idiomatic: On bingzi the emperor held audience in Chongyuan Hall, invested the empress dowager, and had chief minister Su Fengji conduct the ceremony.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，三司使奏：「州縣令錄佐官，請據戶籍多少，量定俸戶：縣三千戶已上，令月十千，主簿八千；

translations.literal: On day xinsi, the commissioner of the three departments memorialized: "For magistrates, recorders, and assistant officials of prefectures and counties, please fix salary households according to the number of registered households: for counties of three thousand households and above, the magistrate ten thousand cash per month and the chief clerk eight thousand;
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi the three departments reported: "Magistrates, recorders, and aides should receive salary households scaled to registered population—for counties of three thousand households or more, the magistrate ten thousand cash monthly and the chief clerk eight thousand;

sentences.zh: 二千戶已上，令月八千，主簿五千；

translations.literal: for two thousand households and above, the magistrate eight thousand per month and the chief clerk five thousand;
translations.idiomatic: for two thousand or more, the magistrate eight thousand and the chief clerk five thousand;

sentences.zh: 二千戶已下，令月六千，主簿四千。

translations.literal: for below two thousand households, the magistrate six thousand per month and the chief clerk four thousand.
translations.idiomatic: below two thousand, the magistrate six thousand and the chief clerk four thousand.

sentences.zh: 每戶月出錢五百，並以管內中等戶充。

translations.literal: Each household shall pay five hundred cash per month, all to be supplied from middling households within the jurisdiction.
translations.idiomatic: Each salary household would pay five hundred cash monthly, drawn from middling taxpayers in the district.

sentences.zh: 錄事參軍、判司俸錢，視州界令佐，取其多者給之，其俸戶與免縣司差役。」

translations.literal: The salaries of the recording adjutant and the judicial administrators shall follow the magistrate and assistants of the prefecture, giving whichever is higher; their salary households shall be exempt from corvée levies imposed by the county office."
translations.idiomatic: Recorder and judicial aides would be paid at whichever county or prefectural rate was higher, and their salary households would be exempt from county corvée."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The memorial was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was approved.

sentences.zh: 八月辛亥，以蒙州城隍神為靈感王，從湖南請也。

translations.literal: In the eighth month, on day xinhai, the city-god of Mengzhou was enfeoffed as King of Spiritual Response, in accordance with a request from Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai in the eighth month Mengzhou's city god was enfeoffed King of Spiritual Response at Hunan's request.

sentences.zh: 時海賊攻州城，州人禱於神，城得不陷，故有是請。

translations.literal: At the time sea bandits were attacking the prefectural city; the people prayed to the god and the city was not taken, and therefore there was this request.
translations.idiomatic: Sea raiders had been besieging the city; after townspeople prayed to the god the walls held, prompting the petition.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，給事中陶穀上言，請停五日內殿轉對。

translations.literal: On day xinyou, Tao Gu, giving-attendant, memorialized requesting to stop the five-day inner-hall rotation memorials.
translations.idiomatic: On xinyou, giving-attendant Tao Gu asked to end the five-day inner-audience rotation of memorials.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The request was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The court agreed.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，以兵部侍郎於德辰為御史中丞，邊蔚為兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: On day renxu, Yu Dechen, Vice Minister of War, was made Censor-in-Chief; Bian Wei was made Vice Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: On renxu, war vice minister Yu Dechen became censor-in-chief and Bian Wei war vice minister.

sentences.zh: 九月辛巳，朗州節度使馬希萼奏請於京師別置邸院。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, on day xinsi, Ma Xie, commissioner of Langzhou, memorialized requesting a separate hostel compound in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: On xinsi in the ninth month Langzhou commissioner Ma Xie asked for a separate lodging compound in the capital.

sentences.zh: 不允。

translations.literal: It was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: The request was denied.

sentences.zh: 是時，希萼與其弟湖南節度使希廣方構鬩墻之怨，故有是請。

translations.literal: At the time Xie and his younger brother Ma Xiguang, commissioner of Hunan, were just then forming a wall-and-moat feud, and therefore there was this request.
translations.idiomatic: Xie and his brother Hunan commissioner Xiguang were then locked in a bitter feud, which explains the petition.

sentences.zh: 帝以湖南已有邸務，不可更置，由是不允，仍命降詔和解焉。

translations.literal: The emperor considered that Hunan already had hostel offices and that another could not be set up; for this reason it was not granted, and he still ordered an edict of reconciliation sent down.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor held that Hunan already had capital lodgings and refused a second compound, but did issue an edict urging the brothers to reconcile.

sentences.zh: 冬十月己亥，帝狩於近郊。

translations.literal: In winter, the tenth month, on day jihai, the emperor hunted near the capital.
translations.idiomatic: On jihai in the tenth month the emperor hunted near the city.

sentences.zh: 丙午，湖南馬希廣遣使上章，且言荊南、淮南、廣南三道結構，欲分割湖、湘，乞聊發兵師，以為援助。

translations.literal: On day bingwu, Ma Xiguang of Hunan dispatched an envoy with a memorial stating that Jingnan, Huainan, and Guangnan circuits were plotting together to partition Hunan and Xiang, and begging that troops be sent briefly as aid.
translations.idiomatic: On bingwu, Hunan's Ma Xiguang sent a memorial claiming that Jingnan, Huainan, and Guangnan were conspiring to carve up Hunan and Xiang and pleading for a short troop deployment.

sentences.zh: 時朝廷方議起軍，會內難，不果行。

translations.literal: At the time the court was just then debating raising an army, but with internal turmoil it did not come to pass.
translations.idiomatic: The court was debating intervention when domestic crisis broke out and the plan was abandoned.

sentences.zh: 丁未，兩浙錢宏俶加諸道兵馬元帥。

translations.literal: On day dingwei, Qian Hongchu of the two Zhes was made overall commander of armies in all circuits.
translations.idiomatic: On dingwei, two-Zhe ruler Qian Hongchu was named commander-in-chief of all circuits.

sentences.zh: 戊申，彰德軍節度使郭謹卒。

translations.literal: On day wushen, Guo Jin, commissioner of the Zhangde army, died.
translations.idiomatic: On wushen, Zhangde commissioner Guo Jin died.

sentences.zh: 癸丑，以前同州節度使張彥赟為相州節度使。

translations.literal: On day guichou, Zhang Yanyun, former commissioner of Tongzhou, was made commissioner of Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On guichou, former Tongzhou commissioner Zhang Yanyun became Xiangzhou commissioner.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，月犯心大星。

translations.literal: On day xinyou, the moon violated the great star of the Heart mansion.
translations.idiomatic: On xinyou the moon crossed the Heart mansion's great star.

sentences.zh: 十一月甲子朔，日有食之。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month, on the first day (day jiazi, new moon), there was a solar eclipse.
translations.idiomatic: The eleventh-month new moon brought a solar eclipse.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，永州唐將軍祠贈太保，從湖南請也。

translations.literal: On day yichou, the shrine of General Tang of Yongzhou was posthumously given Grand Guardian, in accordance with a request from Hunan.
translations.idiomatic: On yichou Yongzhou's General Tang shrine received a posthumous Grand Guardian title at Hunan's request.

sentences.zh: 己巳，日南至，帝御崇元殿受朝賀，仗衛如式。

translations.literal: On day jisi, the winter solstice; the emperor attended the Chongyuan Hall and received congratulatory audience; guards and insignia followed the prescribed forms.
translations.idiomatic: On jisi, the winter solstice, the emperor took congratulations in Chongyuan Hall with full ceremonial guard.

sentences.zh: 辛未，詔侍衛步軍都指揮使王殷將兵屯澶州。

translations.literal: On day xinwei, an edict ordered Wang Yin, overall commander of the palace guard foot soldiers, to lead troops to garrison at Chunzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei an edict sent palace-guard foot commander Wang Yin to encamp at Chunzhou.

sentences.zh: 丙子，誅樞密使楊邠、侍衛都指揮使史宏肇、三司使王章，夷其族。

translations.literal: On day bingzi, the Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs Yang Bin, overall commander of the guard Shi Hongzhao, and commissioner of the three departments Wang Zhang were executed and their clans exterminated.
translations.idiomatic: On bingzi, bureau commissioner Yang Bin, guard commander Shi Hongzhao, and three-departments commissioner Wang Zhang were put to death and their families wiped out.

sentences.zh: 是日平旦，甲士數十人由廣政殿出，至東廡下，害邠等於閣內，死於亂刃之下。

translations.literal: That day at dawn, several tens of armored soldiers came out from the Guangzheng Hall to the eastern veranda and killed Bin and the others inside the side chamber, dying under a chaos of blades.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn that day dozens of soldiers left Guangzheng Hall for the east wing and cut down Bin and his colleagues in a side room.

sentences.zh: 又誅宏肇弟小底軍都虞候宏朗、如京使甄彥奇、內常侍辛從審、楊邠子比部員外郎廷侃、右衛將軍廷偉、右贊善大夫廷倚、王章侄右領衛將軍旻、子婿戶部員外郎張貽肅、樞密院副承宣郭颙、控鶴都虞候高進、侍衛都承局荊南金、三司都勾官柴訓等。

translations.literal: Also executed were Hongzhao's younger brother Honglang, junior army commander of the inner guard; Zhen Yanqi, envoy to the capital; inner attendant Xin Congshen; Yang Bin's son Tingkan, outer court director of the ministry of rites; right guard generals Tingwei and Tingyi, right aide to the heir apparent; Wang Zhang's nephew Min, right guard general; son-in-law Zhang Yisu, outer director of the ministry of revenue; Guo Ying, deputy herald of the bureau; Gao Jin, commander of the crane-control guard; Jingnan Jin of the guard staff bureau; Chai Xun, chief auditor of the three departments, and others.
translations.idiomatic: The purge also took Hongzhao's brother Honglang, capital envoy Zhen Yanqi, attendant Xin Congshen, Yang Bin's sons Tingkan, Tingwei, and Tingyi, Wang Zhang's nephew Min and son-in-law Zhang Yisu, bureau deputy herald Guo Ying, crane-guard commander Gao Jin, guard staff officer Jingnan Jin, and three-departments auditor Chai Xun, among others.

sentences.zh: 分兵收捕邠等家屬及部曲傔從，盡戮之。

translations.literal: Troops were sent separately to seize the families, retainers, and followers of Bin and the others and all were slaughtered.
translations.idiomatic: Separate detachments hunted down their kin, retainers, and clients and killed them all.

sentences.zh: 少頃，樞密承旨聶文進急召宰臣百僚，班於崇元殿，庭宣曰：「楊邠、史宏肇、王章等同謀叛逆，欲危宗社，並斬之，與卿等同慶。」

translations.literal: Shortly after, bureau herald Nie Wenjin urgently summoned the chief ministers and the hundred officials to line up in the Chongyuan Hall; in the courtyard he proclaimed: "Yang Bin, Shi Hongzhao, Wang Zhang, and others together plotted rebellion and wished to endanger the altars of state; all have been beheaded—rejoice with Us.
translations.idiomatic: Moments later bureau herald Nie Wenjin assembled the ministers in Chongyuan Hall and announced from the courtyard, "Yang Bin, Shi Hongzhao, and Wang Zhang had plotted treason, had been executed, and that all should rejoice."

sentences.zh: 班退，召諸軍將校至萬歲殿，帝親諭史宏肇等欲謀逆亂之狀，且言：「宏肇等欺朕年幼，專權擅命，使汝輩常懷憂恐，自此朕自與汝等為主，必無橫憂也。」

translations.literal: When the audience withdrew, military commanders were summoned to the Hall of Ten Thousand Years; the emperor personally explained the signs of Hongzhao and the others' intended rebellion, and said: "Hongzhao and the others deceived Us while We were young, monopolized authority and issued orders on their own, so that you constantly lived in fear; from now on We Ourselves will be master for you—there will certainly be no sudden calamity."
translations.idiomatic: After dismissal he gathered commanders in Wansui Hall, accused Hongzhao's party of treason, and said, "They bullied a young emperor, seized power, and kept you in fear—from now on I rule for you myself and you need not dread sudden ruin."

sentences.zh: 諸軍將校拜謝而退。

translations.literal: The military commanders bowed in thanks and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: The commanders bowed and left.

sentences.zh: 召前任節度使、刺史、統軍等上殿諭之。

translations.literal: Former commissioners, prefects, and army supervisors were summoned to the hall and instructed.
translations.idiomatic: Former commissioners, prefects, and army inspectors were called in and addressed.

sentences.zh: 帝遣軍士守捉宮城諸門，比近日旰，朝臣步出宮門而去。

translations.literal: The emperor sent soldiers to guard all the gates of the palace city; compared with recent days it was already dusk when courtiers walked out through the palace gates.
translations.idiomatic: Troops sealed the palace gates; courtiers did not leave until near dusk, far later than usual.

sentences.zh: 是日晴霽無雲，而昏霧濛濛，有如微雨，人情惴恐。

translations.literal: That day was clear without clouds, yet a dim mist hung hazy as if in light rain, and people's hearts were fearful.
translations.idiomatic: Though the sky was clear, a dull haze like drizzle hung over the city and fear spread among the people.

sentences.zh: 日將午，載楊邠等十餘屍，分暴於南北市。

translations.literal: As the sun neared noon, more than ten corpses including Yang Bin's were loaded and publicly exposed in the northern and southern markets.
translations.idiomatic: Near noon a dozen-odd bodies, including Yang Bin's, were paraded and displayed in both markets.

sentences.zh: 是日，帝遣腹心賫密詔往澶州、鄴都，令澶州節度使李洪義誅侍衛步軍都指揮使王殷，令鄴都屯駐護聖左廂都指揮使郭崇、奉國左廂都指揮使曹英害樞密使郭威及宣徽使王峻。

translations.literal: That day the emperor sent a trusted agent bearing a secret edict to Chunzhou and Yedu, ordering Chunzhou commissioner Li Hongyi to kill foot-commander Wang Yin, and ordering Guo Chong, commander of the left wing of the guard-for-the-sacred, and Cao Ying, commander of the left wing of the nation-supporting army, to kill bureau commissioner Guo Wei and palace commissioner Wang Jun.
translations.idiomatic: That day he sent a secret edict to Chunzhou and Yedu ordering Li Hongyi to kill Wang Yin and ordering Guo Chong and Cao Ying to murder Guo Wei and Wang Jun.

sentences.zh: 急詔鄆州高行周、青州符彥卿、永興郭從義、兗州慕容彥超、同州薛懷讓、鄭州吳虔裕、陳州李穀等赴闕。

translations.literal: Urgent edicts summoned Gao Xingzhou of Yunzhou, Fu Yanqing of Qingzhou, Guo Congyi of Yongxing, Murong Yanchao of Yanzhou, Xue Huairang of Tongzhou, Wu Qianyu of Zhengzhou, Li Gu of Chenzhou, and others to court.
translations.idiomatic: Emergency orders called Gao Xingzhou, Fu Yanqing, Guo Congyi, Murong Yanchao, Xue Huairang, Wu Qianyu, Li Gu, and others to the capital.

sentences.zh: 以宰臣蘇逢吉權知樞密院事，前青州劉銖權知開封府事，侍衛馬軍都指揮使李洪建判侍衛司事，內客省使閻晉卿權侍衛馬軍都指揮使。

translations.literal: The chief minister Su Fengji was given acting authority over the bureau; Liu Zhu of former Qingzhou was given acting authority over Kaifeng; Li Hongjian, horse-commander of the guard, was assigned to manage guard affairs; inner-service commissioner Yan Jinqing was made acting horse-commander of the guard.
translations.idiomatic: Su Fengji took acting charge of the bureau, former Qingzhou commissioner Liu Zhu acting Kaifeng mayor, guard horse commander Li Hongjian managing guard affairs, and inner-service commissioner Yan Jinqing acting horse commander.

sentences.zh: 丁丑，澶州節度使李洪義受得密詔，知事不克，乃引使人見王殷。

translations.literal: On day dingchou, Li Hongyi, commissioner of Chunzhou, received the secret edict and knew the affair could not succeed; he therefore led the envoy to see Wang Yin.
translations.idiomatic: On dingchou, Chunzhou commissioner Li Hongyi received the secret edict, saw the plot would fail, and brought the envoy to Wang Yin.

sentences.zh: 殷與洪義遣本州副使陳光穗賫所受密詔，馳至鄴都。

translations.literal: Yin and Hongyi sent the prefectural vice commissioner Chen Guangsu bearing the secret edict they had received, galloping to Yedu.
translations.idiomatic: Yin and Hongyi sent vice commissioner Chen Guangsu with the edict at full speed to Yedu.

sentences.zh: 〈（《宋史》：少帝遣供奉官孟業賫密詔，令洪義殺王殷。

translations.literal: (From the History of Song: the young emperor sent the tribute officer Meng Ye bearing a secret edict ordering Hongyi to kill Wang Yin.
translations.idiomatic: (From the History of Song: the young emperor sent tribute officer Meng Ye with a secret edict for Hongyi to kill Wang Yin.

sentences.zh: 洪義素怯懦，慮殷覺，遷延不敢發，遽引業見殷。

translations.literal: Hongyi had always been timid; fearing Yin would detect it, he delayed and did not dare act, but abruptly led Ye to see Yin.
translations.idiomatic: Hongyi was by nature cowardly, feared discovery, hesitated, then abruptly presented Ye to Yin.

sentences.zh: 殷乃錮業，送密詔於周祖。）〉

translations.literal: Yin then imprisoned Ye and sent the secret edict to the Zhou founder.)〉
translations.idiomatic: Yin imprisoned Ye and forwarded the secret edict to the Zhou founder.)〉

sentences.zh: 郭威得之，即召王峻、郭崇、曹英及諸軍將校，至牙署視詔，兼告楊、史諸公冤枉之狀，且曰：「汝等當奉行詔旨，斷予首以報天子，自取功名。」

translations.literal: When Guo Wei received it, he immediately summoned Wang Jun, Guo Chong, Cao Ying, and the military commanders to the headquarters office to view the edict, and also told them of the wrongful deaths of Yang and Shi and the others, saying: "You should carry out the edict's command, cut off Our head to report to the Son of Heaven, and take merit for yourselves."
translations.idiomatic: Guo Wei summoned Wang Jun, Guo Chong, Cao Ying, and his commanders, showed them the edict, described how Yang Bin and Shi Hongzhao had been wronged, and said, "Obey the edict—cut off my head for the emperor and win your reward."

sentences.zh: 郭崇等與諸將校前曰：「此事必非聖意，即是李業等竊發，假如此輩便握權柄，國得安乎！

translations.literal: Guo Chong and the commanders stepped forward and said: "This affair is certainly not the sage emperor's intent; it must be Li Ye and others acting in secret. If such men were to grasp power, could the state be secure!
translations.idiomatic: Guo Chong and the others stepped forward: "This cannot be the emperor's will—it must be Li Ye's clique. If they hold power, how can the realm be safe?

sentences.zh: 事可陳論，何須自棄，致千載之下被此惡名。

translations.literal: The matter can be explained; why must you abandon yourselves and leave a foul name for a thousand years below?
translations.idiomatic: The case can be argued—why destroy yourselves and earn infamy for ages?

sentences.zh: 崇等願從公入朝，面自洗雪。」

translations.literal: Chong and the others wish to follow the lord into court and personally clear themselves."
translations.idiomatic: Chong and the others asked to follow him to court and clear their names in person."

sentences.zh: 於是將校等請威入朝，以除君側之惡，共安天下。

translations.literal: Thereupon the commanders asked Wei to enter court to remove evil beside the ruler and together pacify the realm.
translations.idiomatic: The commanders then urged Wei to march on the capital, purge the emperor's evil counselors, and settle the realm.

sentences.zh: 〈（《東都事略》：漢隱帝遣使害太祖，魏仁浦曰：「公有大功於朝廷，握強兵，臨重鎮，以讒見疑，豈可坐而待斃！」

translations.literal: (From the Summary of Affairs in the Eastern Capital: Emperor Yin of Han sent envoys to kill the founding ancestor. Wei Renpu said: "You have great merit toward the court, hold a strong army, and face a weighty post; because of slander you are suspected—how can you sit and await death!"
translations.idiomatic: (From the Summary of Affairs in the Eastern Capital: Emperor Yin sent agents to kill Guo Wei. Wei Renpu said, "You have great service, command a powerful army, and hold a key post—slandered and suspected, how can you sit and die?"

sentences.zh: 教以易其語，雲誅將士，以激怒眾心。

translations.literal: He taught them to change the wording to say execute the officers, in order to inflame popular feeling.
translations.idiomatic: He told them to alter the wording to call for executing the soldiers and stir popular anger.

sentences.zh: 太祖納其言。）〉

translations.literal: The founding ancestor accepted his advice.)〉
translations.idiomatic: Guo Wei took his advice.)〉

sentences.zh: 翌日，郭威以眾南行。

translations.literal: The next day, Guo Wei led his host south.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Guo Wei marched south.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，鄴兵至澶州。

translations.literal: On day wuyin, the Yedu army reached Chunzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin the Yedu force reached Chunzhou.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，至滑州，節度使宋延渥開門迎降。

translations.literal: On day gengchen, they reached Huazhou; commissioner Song Yanwo opened the gates and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: On gengchen they reached Huazhou; commissioner Song Yanwo opened the gates in surrender.

sentences.zh: 是日，詔前開封尹侯益、前鄜州節度使張彥超、權侍衛馬軍都指揮使閻晉卿、鄭州防禦使吳虔裕等，率禁軍赴澶州守捉。

translations.literal: That day, an edict ordered former Kaifeng mayor Hou Yi, former Bin commissioner Zhang Yanchao, acting guard horse commander Yan Jinqing, Zhengzhou defender Wu Qianyu, and others to lead the palace guard to Chunzhou to intercept.
translations.idiomatic: That day an edict sent former Kaifeng mayor Hou Yi, former Bin commissioner Zhang Yanchao, acting guard horse commander Yan Jinqing, Zhengzhou defender Wu Qianyu, and others with the palace guard to hold Chunzhou.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，帝之小豎嵒脫自北回。

translations.literal: The emperor's young attendant Yan Tuo returned from the north.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's young attendant Yan Tuo returned from the north.

sentences.zh: 先是，帝遣嵒脫偵鄴軍所至，為遊騎所獲，郭威即遣回，因令附奏赴闕之意，仍以密奏置嵒脫衣領中。

translations.literal: Earlier, the emperor had sent Yan Tuo to spy on where the Yedu army was going; he was captured by roaming scouts. Guo Wei immediately sent him back, thereby ordering him to attach a memorial of his intent to proceed to court, and also placed a secret memorial in Yan Tuo's collar.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had sent Yan Tuo to scout the Yedu army; scouts seized him, but Guo Wei sent him back with a collar-hidden memorial stating his intent to come to court.

sentences.zh: 帝覽奏，即召李業示之，聶文進、郭允明在傍，懼形於色。

translations.literal: The emperor viewed the memorial and immediately summoned Li Ye to show it; Nie Wenjin and Guo Yunming were beside him, fear showing on their faces.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor read it, summoned Li Ye, and Nie Wenjin and Guo Yunming beside him showed their fear.

sentences.zh: 初議車駕幸澶州，及聞鄴兵已至河上，乃止。

translations.literal: At first they discussed the imperial carriage going to Chunzhou, but on hearing the Yedu army had already reached the river, they stopped.
translations.idiomatic: They had planned an imperial visit to Chunzhou but halted when news came that the Yedu army had reached the Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 帝大懼，私謂宰臣竇貞固等曰：「昨來之事，太草草耳！」

translations.literal: The emperor was greatly afraid and privately said to chief minister Dou Zhengu and others: "Yesterday's affair was far too rash!"
translations.idiomatic: Terrified, he told chief minister Dou Zhengu, "Yesterday's business was far too rash!"

sentences.zh: 李業等請帝傾府庫以給諸軍，宰相蘇禹珪以為未可。

translations.literal: Li Ye and others asked the emperor to empty the treasury to pay the armies; chief minister Su Yugui thought it could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: Li Ye urged emptying the treasury for the troops; Su Yugui objected.

sentences.zh: 業拜禹珪於帝前，曰：「相公且為官家，莫惜府庫。」

translations.literal: Ye bowed to Yugui before the emperor and said: "Minister, think of the ruler—do not be sparing of the treasury."
translations.idiomatic: Ye bowed to Yugui before the emperor: "Minister, serve the ruler—spare not the treasury."

sentences.zh: 遂下令侍衛軍人給二十緡，下軍各給十緡，其北來將士亦準此。

translations.literal: Thereupon orders were issued: palace guard soldiers twenty strings of cash each, lower guard ten strings each, and northern soldiers likewise.
translations.idiomatic: Orders followed: twenty strings for palace guards, ten for lower guards, the same for northern troops.

sentences.zh: 仍遣北來將士在營子弟各賫家問，向北諭之。

translations.literal: Northern soldiers' sons and younger brothers still in camp were also each sent family inquiries to be carried north and announced to them.
translations.idiomatic: Sons and brothers of northern troops in camp were sent family messages to carry north.

sentences.zh: 壬午，鄴軍至封丘。

translations.literal: On day renwu, the Yedu army reached Fengqiu.
translations.idiomatic: On renwu the Yedu army reached Fengqiu.

sentences.zh: 慕容彥超自鎮馳至，帝遂以軍旅之事委之。

translations.literal: Murong Yanchao hurried from his post; the emperor then entrusted military affairs to him.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Yanchao raced from his province and the emperor put the campaign in his hands.

sentences.zh: 〈（《宋史·侯益傳》云：周太祖起兵，隱帝議出師禦之。

translations.literal: (From the biography of Hou Yi in the History of Song: when the Zhou founding ancestor raised troops, Emperor Yin discussed sending an army to resist.
translations.idiomatic: (From the History of Song, biography of Hou Yi: when Guo Wei rebelled, Emperor Yin debated marching against him.

sentences.zh: 益獻計曰：「王者無敵於天下，兵不宜輕出，況大名戍卒，家屬盡在京城，不如閉關以挫其銳，遣其母妻發降以招之，可不戰而定。」

translations.literal: Yi presented a plan: "A king is without enemy under Heaven; troops should not lightly go out. Moreover the Daming garrison soldiers all have families in the capital—it is better to close the passes to blunt their edge, send out their mothers and wives with surrender messages to summon them, and they can be settled without battle.
translations.idiomatic: Yi proposed: "The Son of Heaven has no peer—armies should not march lightly. Daming troops have kin in the capital; close the passes, send their families with surrender appeals, and win without fighting."

sentences.zh: 慕容彥超以為益衰老，作懦夫計，沮之。）〉

translations.literal: Murong Yanchao considered Yi old and offering a coward's plan, and obstructed it.)〉
translations.idiomatic: Murong Yanchao called Yi senile and his plan cowardly, and blocked it.)〉

sentences.zh: 彥超謂帝曰：「陛下勿憂，臣當生致其魁首。」

translations.literal: Yanchao said to the emperor: "Your Majesty need not worry; your subject will capture their leader alive.
translations.idiomatic: Yanchao told the emperor, "Do not worry, Majesty—I will take their leader alive."

sentences.zh: 彥超退，見聶文進，詢北來兵數及將校名氏，文進告之。

translations.literal: Yanchao withdrew and saw Nie Wenjin, inquiring about the numbers of northern troops and the names of commanders; Wenjin told him.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward Yanchao asked Nie Wenjin the northern army's strength and commanders.

sentences.zh: 彥超懼，曰：「大是劇賊，不宜輕耳！」

translations.literal: Yanchao feared and said: "They are fierce rebels indeed—not to be taken lightly!
translations.idiomatic: Yanchao grew afraid: "These are fierce enemies—not to be treated lightly!"

sentences.zh: 又遣袁鳷、劉重進、王知則等出師，以繼前軍。

translations.literal: He also sent Yuan Ji, Liu Zhongjin, Wang Zhize, and others to take the field to follow the earlier army.
translations.idiomatic: He sent Yuan Ji, Liu Zhongjin, Wang Zhize, and others to reinforce the vanguard.

sentences.zh: 慕容彥超以大軍駐於七里郊，掘塹以自衛，都下率坊市出酒食以餉軍。

translations.literal: Murong Yanchao stationed his great army at the Seven-Li suburb, dug trenches for self-defense, and the capital's wards and markets turned out wine and food to feed the army.
translations.idiomatic: Yanchao encamped at Seven-Li, dug trenches, and the city markets supplied food and drink.

sentences.zh: 癸未，車駕勞軍，即日還宮。

translations.literal: On day guimao, the imperial carriage went to comfort the army and that day returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: On guimao the emperor reviewed the troops and returned the same day.

sentences.zh: 翌日，慕容彥超揚言曰：「官家宮中無事，明日再出，觀臣破賊。」

translations.literal: The next day Murong Yanchao proclaimed: "All is well in the palace; tomorrow the ruler will come out again to watch your subject break the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Next day Yanchao announced, "The palace is secure; tomorrow the emperor will watch me break the rebels."

sentences.zh: 甲申，車駕復出，幸七里店軍營。

translations.literal: On day jiashen, the imperial carriage again went out and visited the Seven-Li camp.
translations.idiomatic: On jiashen the emperor again visited the Seven-Li camp.

sentences.zh: 王師陣於劉子陂，與鄴軍相望。

translations.literal: The imperial army formed at Liuzi slope, facing the Yedu army across the distance.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial forces formed at Liuzi Slope opposite the Yedu army.

sentences.zh: 太后以帝至晚在外，遣中使謂聶文進曰：「賊軍在近，大須用意！」

translations.literal: The empress dowager, because the emperor was out late, sent a palace envoy to tell Nie Wenjin: "The rebel army is near—you must be very careful!
translations.idiomatic: The dowager, worried the emperor was out late, told Nie Wenjin, "The rebels are close—take care!"

sentences.zh: 文進曰：「有臣在，必不失策，縱有一百個郭威，亦當生擒之耳！」

translations.literal: Wenjin said: "With your subject here, policy will not fail; even a hundred Guo Weis would be captured alive!"
translations.idiomatic: Wenjin replied, "I am here—we cannot fail; even a hundred Guo Weis I would seize alive!"

sentences.zh: 彥超輕脫，先擊北軍，郭威命何福進、王彥超、李筠等大合騎以乘之。

translations.literal: Yanchao was rash; he struck the northern army first. Guo Wei ordered He Fujin, Wang Yanchao, Li Yun, and others to mass cavalry and press them.
translations.idiomatic: Yanchao rashly attacked the northern wing; Guo Wei sent He Fujin, Wang Yanchao, Li Yun, and others with massed cavalry against him.

sentences.zh: 彥超退卻，死者百餘人，於是諸軍奪氣，稍稍奔於北軍。

translations.literal: Yanchao fell back; more than a hundred died, and then the armies lost heart and gradually ran to the northern army.
translations.idiomatic: Yanchao retreated with a hundred-odd dead; imperial morale collapsed and men drifted to Guo Wei.

sentences.zh: 吳虔裕、張彥超等相繼而去，慕容彥超以部下十數騎奔兗州。

translations.literal: Wu Qianyu, Zhang Yanchao, and others left in succession; Murong Yanchao fled to Yanzhou with a dozen-odd riders of his command.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Qianyu and Zhang Yanchao fled; Murong Yanchao escaped to Yanzhou with a dozen horsemen.

sentences.zh: 是夜，帝與宰臣從官宿於野次，侯益、焦繼勛潛奔鄴軍。

translations.literal: That night the emperor and chief ministers and attendants lodged in the open field; Hou Yi and Jiao Jixun secretly fled to the Yedu army.
translations.idiomatic: That night the emperor camped in the open with his ministers; Hou Yi and Jiao Jixun defected to Guo Wei.

sentences.zh: 乙酉旦，帝策馬至元化門，劉銖在門上，問帝左右：「兵馬何在？」

translations.literal: At dawn on yiyou the emperor spurred his horse to the Yuanhua Gate; Liu Zhu was on the gate and asked the emperor's attendants: "Where are the troops?"
translations.idiomatic: At dawn on yiyou the emperor rode to Yuanhua Gate; Liu Zhu on the wall asked his escort, "Where is the army?"

sentences.zh: 乃射左右。

translations.literal: Then he shot the attendants.
translations.idiomatic: Then he shot at the attendants.

sentences.zh: 帝回，與蘇逢吉、郭允明詣西北村舍，郭允明知事不濟，乃剚刃於帝而崩，時年二十。

translations.literal: The emperor turned back and went with Su Fengji and Guo Yunming to a village house northwest of the city; Guo Yunming, knowing affairs could not succeed, drew his blade on the emperor and he perished, aged twenty.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor turned back with Su Fengji and Guo Yunming to a northwest village; Yunming, seeing all was lost, killed the emperor with his blade. He was twenty.

sentences.zh: 蘇逢吉、郭允明皆自殺。

translations.literal: Su Fengji and Guo Yunming both killed themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Su Fengji and Guo Yunming also killed themselves.

sentences.zh: 是日，周太祖自迎春門入，諸軍大掠，煙火四發，翌日至晡方定。

translations.literal: That day the Zhou founding ancestor entered through the Yingchun Gate; the armies plundered greatly, fires blazed on four sides, and only by the next day's dusk was it settled.
translations.idiomatic: That day Guo Wei entered by Yingchun Gate; troops looted until fires burned everywhere and order returned only by the next dusk.

sentences.zh: 前滑州節度使白再筠為亂兵所害，吏部侍郎張允墜屋而死。

translations.literal: Bai Zaiyun, former Huazhou commissioner, was killed by mutinous soldiers; Vice Minister of Personnel Zhang Yun fell from a house and died.
translations.idiomatic: Former Huazhou commissioner Bai Zaiyun was killed by mutineers; personnel vice minister Zhang Yun fell from a building and died.

sentences.zh: 周太祖既入京城，命有司遷帝梓宮於太平宮。

translations.literal: After the Zhou founding ancestor had entered the capital, he ordered the relevant offices to move the emperor's coffin to the Taiping Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Once in the capital, Guo Wei ordered the emperor's coffin moved to Taiping Palace.

sentences.zh: 或曰：「可依魏高貴鄉公故事，以公禮葬之。」

translations.literal: Someone said: "It may follow the precedent of the noble village lord of Wei and bury him with ducal rites."
translations.idiomatic: Some said, "Follow the Wei noble village lord precedent and bury him with ducal rites."

sentences.zh: 周祖曰：「予顛沛之中，不能護衛至尊，以至於此，若又貶降，人謂我何！」

translations.literal: The Zhou founder said: "In Our wandering distress We could not protect the exalted ruler and it came to this; if We also demote him, what will people say of Us!"
translations.idiomatic: Guo Wei said, "In my wanderings I could not protect the emperor and it came to this—if I demote him too, what will men say of me?"

sentences.zh: 於是詔擇日舉哀，命前宗正卿劉皞主喪。

translations.literal: Thereupon an edict chose a day for mourning and ordered former director of the imperial clan Liu Hao to preside.
translations.idiomatic: An edict set a mourning day and named former imperial-clan director Liu Hao to direct the rites.

sentences.zh: 丙戌，太后誥曰：

translations.literal: On day bingxu, the empress dowager's proclamation stated:
translations.idiomatic: On bingxu the dowager issued a proclamation:

sentences.zh: 高祖皇帝翦亂除兇，變家為國，救生靈於塗炭，創王業於艱難，甫定寰區，遽遺弓劍。

translations.literal: The founding emperor Gaozu cut disorder and removed the violent, changed the family into a state, saved the living from charcoal and fire, and created royal enterprise amid hardship; he had just settled the realm when he suddenly left bow and sword.
translations.idiomatic: Founding emperor Gaozu ended chaos, made the house a state, rescued the people, and built the dynasty in hardship; he had barely settled the realm when he died.

sentences.zh: 樞密使郭威楊邠、侍衛使史弘肇、三司使王章親承顧命，輔立少君，協力同心，安邦定國。

translations.literal: Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs Guo Wei, Yang Bin, guard commander Shi Hongzhao, and three-departments commissioner Wang Zhang personally received the dying charge, assisted and established the young ruler, and with combined strength pacified the state.
translations.idiomatic: Bureau commissioner Guo Wei, Yang Bin, guard commander Shi Hongzhao, and three-departments commissioner Wang Zhang received the deathbed charge, installed the young ruler, and together stabilized the realm.

sentences.zh: 旋屬四方多事，三叛連衡，吳、蜀內侵，契丹啟釁，烝黎兇懼，宗社阽危。

translations.literal: Soon thereafter the four quarters had many affairs; the three rebellions linked in alliance; Wu and Shu invaded within; the Khitan opened provocation; the people were fierce with fear and the altars were in peril.
translations.idiomatic: Soon rebellions linked, Wu and Shu invaded, the Khitan raided, and the people and altars trembled.

sentences.zh: 郭威授任專征，提戈進討，躬當矢石，盡掃煙塵，外寇蕩平，中原寧謐。

translations.literal: Guo Wei received appointment for a dedicated campaign, raised the spear and advanced, himself met stones and arrows, swept away all dust and smoke, outer enemies were pacified, and the central plains were tranquil.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Wei took command, fought in person, swept the field, pacified foreign enemies, and quieted the heartland.

sentences.zh: 復以強敵未殄，邊塞多艱，允賴寶臣，往臨大鄴，疆場有藩籬之固，朝廷寬宵旰之憂。

translations.literal: Again, because a strong enemy was not destroyed and the borders had many hardships, reliance was placed on a treasured minister to go to great Yedu; the frontier had the solidity of a fence and the court was eased of night-watch anxiety.
translations.idiomatic: With foes still active he was sent to Yedu to secure the frontier and ease the court's vigilance.

sentences.zh: 不謂兇豎連謀，群小得志，密藏鋒刃，竊發殿庭，已殺害其忠良，方奏聞於少主，無辜受戮，有口稱冤。

translations.literal: Who would have thought vicious fellows would link in conspiracy and petty men would gain their wish, secretly hiding blades and stealing to strike in the palace hall—they had already killed loyal ministers and were just then reporting to the young ruler; the innocent received slaughter and had mouths that called it injustice.
translations.idiomatic: Yet villains conspired, hid blades in the hall, murdered loyal ministers, and lied to the young emperor; innocents were slaughtered and cried injustice.

sentences.zh: 而又潛差使臣，矯賫宣命，謀害樞密使郭威、宣徽使王峻、侍衛步軍都指揮使王殷等。

translations.literal: Moreover they secretly sent envoys, falsely bearing imperial orders, plotting to kill bureau commissioner Guo Wei, palace commissioner Wang Jun, and guard foot commander Wang Yin.
translations.idiomatic: They also sent secret agents with forged orders to kill Guo Wei, Wang Jun, and Wang Yin.

sentences.zh: 人知無罪，天不助奸。

translations.literal: People knew they were without crime; Heaven did not aid the wicked.
translations.idiomatic: Men knew they were guiltless; Heaven would not help traitors.

sentences.zh: 今者，郭威，王峻，澶州節度使李洪義，前曹州防禦使何福進，前復州防禦使王彥超，前博州刺史李筠，北面行營馬步都指揮使郭崇，步軍都指揮使曹英，護聖都指揮使白重贊、索萬進、田景鹹、樊愛能、李萬全、史彥超，奉國都指揮使張鐸、王暉、胡立，弩手指揮使何赟等，徑領兵師，來安社稷。

translations.literal: Now Guo Wei, Wang Jun, Chunzhou commissioner Li Hongyi, former Caozhou defender He Fujin, former Fuzhou defender Wang Yanchao, former Bozhou prefect Li Yun, northern field horse-and-foot commander Guo Chong, foot commander Cao Ying, guard-for-the-sacred commanders Bai Chongzan, Suo Wanjin, Tian Jingxian, Fan Aineng, Li Wanquan, Shi Yanchao, nation-supporting commanders Zhang Duo, Wang Hui, Hu Li, crossbow commander He Yun, and others directly led armies to settle the altars.
translations.idiomatic: Now Guo Wei, Wang Jun, Li Hongyi, military commissioner of Chanzhou, former defenders He Fujin of Caozhou and Wang Yanchao of Fuzhou, former Bozhou prefect Li Yun, northern field horse-and-foot commander Guo Chong, infantry commander Cao Ying, Guarding-the-Sacred commanders Bai Chongzan, Suo Wanjin, Tian Jingxian, Fan Aineng, Li Wanquan, and Shi Yanchao, Serving-the-State commanders Zhang Duo, Wang Hui, and Hu Li, crossbow commander He Yun, and others have led their armies directly here to secure the altars of state.

sentences.zh: 逆黨皇城使李業、內客省使閻晉卿、樞密都承旨聶文進、飛龍使後贊、翰林茶酒使郭允明等，脅君於大內，出戰於近郊，及至力窮，遂行弒逆，冤憤之極，今古未聞。

translations.literal: The rebel party—palace envoy Li Ye, inner-service commissioner Yan Jinqing, bureau herald Nie Wenjin, flying-dragon commissioner Hou Zan, Hanlin tea-and-wine commissioner Guo Yunming, and others—coerced the ruler in the inner palace and went out to battle in the near suburbs; when their strength was exhausted they then carried out regicide; the extremity of wronged rage is unheard of in past and present.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels Li Ye, Yan Jinqing, Nie Wenjin, Hou Zan, Guo Yunming, and others coerced the emperor, fought at the suburbs, and when spent murdered him—a crime unheard of in history.

sentences.zh: 今則兇黨既除，群情共悅。

translations.literal: Now the vicious party has been removed and all hearts rejoice together.
translations.idiomatic: Now the villains are gone and all hearts rejoice.

sentences.zh: 神器不可以無主，萬機不可以久曠，宜擇賢君，以安天下。

translations.literal: The sacred vessel cannot be without a master; the myriad affairs cannot long be vacant—an worthy ruler should be chosen to settle the realm.
translations.idiomatic: The throne cannot stay empty; affairs cannot wait—choose a worthy ruler to settle the realm.

sentences.zh: 河東節度使崇、許州節度使信，皆高祖之弟，徐州節度使赟、開封尹承勛，高祖之男，俱列盤維，皆居屏翰，宜令文武百辟，議擇嗣君，以承大統雲。

translations.literal: Hedong commissioner Chong and Xuzhou commissioner Xin are both younger brothers of Gaozu; Xuzhou commissioner Yun and Kaifeng mayor Chengxun are sons of Gaozu—all are imperial kin and screen the state; civil and military officials should deliberate and choose a successor to receive the great succession.
translations.idiomatic: Hedong's Chong and Xu's Xin are Gaozu's brothers; Xu's Yun and Kaifeng's Chengxun are his sons—all imperial kin who should be considered for succession.

sentences.zh: 樞密使郭威以蕭墻變起，宗祏無奉，率群臣候太后，請定所立，且言：「開封尹承勛，高祖皇帝之愛子也，請立為嗣。」

translations.literal: Bureau commissioner Guo Wei, because trouble arose within the curtained wall and the ancestral temple had no one to receive sacrifice, led the civil and military officials to wait on the dowager and request fixing who should be established, and said: "Kaifeng mayor Chengxun is the founding emperor's beloved son—please establish him as successor.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Wei, with no heir at the altars, asked the dowager to choose a successor and said, "Kaifeng mayor Chengxun is Gaozu's beloved son—please establish him as successor."

sentences.zh: 太后告以承勛羸病日久，不能自舉。

translations.literal: The dowager reported that Chengxun had long been ill with weakness and could not rise.
translations.idiomatic: The dowager said Chengxun had been gravely ill and could not govern.

sentences.zh: 周太祖與諸將請視承勛起居，及視之，方信，遂議立高祖從子、徐州節度使赟為嗣。

translations.literal: The Zhou founding ancestor and the generals asked to view Chengxun's condition; when they viewed it they believed it, and then deliberated establishing Gaozu's younger brother's son, Xuzhou commissioner Yun, as successor.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Wei and the generals inspected Chengxun, found it true, and settled on Gaozu's nephew, Xuzhou commissioner Yun.

sentences.zh: 己丑，太后誥曰：「天未悔禍，喪亂宏多，嗣王幼沖，群兇蔽惑，構奸謀於造次，縱毒蠆於斯須，將相大臣，連頸受戮，股肱良佐，無罪見屠，行路咨嗟，群心扼腕，則高祖之洪烈將墜於地。

translations.literal: On day jichou, the dowager's proclamation stated: "Heaven has not yet repented of calamity; disorder and ruin are many; the successor king is young; vicious fellows deceived him; they formed wicked plots in haste and released poison in a moment; ministers and great officials were slaughtered neck to neck; loyal assistants were killed without crime; travelers sighed and all hearts clutched their wrists—then the founding emperor's great enterprise would fall to earth.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou the dowager proclaimed: "Heaven has not yet repented of calamity; disorder and ruin are many; the young successor is deceived; vicious men formed wicked plots in haste; ministers and loyal assistants were slaughtered without cause; travelers sighed and hearts clutched their wrists—Gaozu's great enterprise would fall to earth.

sentences.zh: 賴大臣郭威等，激揚忠義，拯濟顛危，除惡蔓以無遺，俾綴旒之不絕。

translations.literal: Relying on great ministers Guo Wei and others, who roused loyal righteousness and rescued peril, removed the wicked root without remnant, and kept the suspended pearl from being cut off.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Wei and loyal ministers had crushed the villains and preserved the line.

sentences.zh: 宗祧事重，纘繼才難，既聞將相之謀，復考蓍龜之兆，天人協贊，社稷是依。

translations.literal: The ancestral temple affair is weighty and succession is hard; having heard the ministers' and generals' plan and again examined the tortoise and milfoil omens, Heaven and men together approve and the altars rely on it.
translations.idiomatic: With omens and ministers aligned, succession must proceed.

sentences.zh: 徐州節度使赟，稟上聖之資，抱中和之德，先皇如子，鐘愛特深，固可以子育兆民，君臨萬國，宜令所司擇日備法駕奉迎即皇帝位。

translations.literal: Xuzhou commissioner Yun possesses the substance of the supreme sage and embraces the virtue of centrality and harmony; the former emperor treated him as a son and loved him especially deep—he can certainly nurture the myriad people and rule the myriad states; the relevant offices should choose a day, prepare the imperial equipage, and welcome him to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Xuzhou commissioner Yun, deeply loved by the late emperor, should be welcomed to the throne on a chosen day.

sentences.zh: 於戲！

translations.literal: Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Alas!

sentences.zh: 神器至重，天步方艱，致理保邦，不可以不敬，貽謀聽政，不可以不勤，允執厥中，祗膺景命。」

translations.literal: The sacred vessel is supremely weighty; the heavenly step is just then difficult; to bring order and preserve the state cannot but be reverent; to hand down plans and hear government cannot but be diligent; hold the center and reverently receive the bright mandate."
translations.idiomatic: The throne is weighty, the times hard—rule with reverence and diligence and hold the center."

sentences.zh: 是日，遣前太師馮道等往徐奉迎。

translations.literal: That day former Grand Preceptor Feng Dao and others were sent to Xu to welcome him.
translations.idiomatic: That day former grand preceptor Feng Dao was sent to Xu to escort him.

sentences.zh: 周太祖以嗣君未至，萬機不可暫曠，率群臣請太后臨朝，誥答曰：「昨以奸邪構釁，亂我邦家，勛德效忠，剪除兇慝，俯從人欲，已立嗣君，宗社危而再安，紀綱壞而復振。

translations.literal: Because the successor ruler had not arrived and the myriad affairs could not briefly be vacant, the Zhou founding ancestor led the civil and military officials to ask the dowager to preside at court; the proclamation answered: "Yesterday vicious traitors formed calamity and disturbed Our state; meritorious virtue showed loyalty and cut down the vicious; bowing to human desire, a successor ruler has already been established; the altars were perilous and again secure, the statutes broken and again restored.
translations.idiomatic: With the heir not yet arrived, Guo Wei asked the dowager to rule temporarily; her proclamation answered: "Yesterday vicious traitors disturbed our state; loyal merit cut down the villains; bowing to popular will a successor was established; the altars were perilous and again secure, statutes broken and again restored.

sentences.zh: 皇帝法駕未至，庶事方殷，百辟上言，請予蒞政，宜允輿議，權總萬機，止於浹旬，即復明辟」云。

translations.literal: The emperor's imperial equipage has not arrived and the myriad affairs are still pressing; the hundred officials above speak and request that We preside over government—it should accord with public deliberation and temporarily total the myriad affairs, stopping at ten days, then restore the bright ruler."
translations.idiomatic: Until the emperor arrives she would temporarily rule the myriad affairs for ten days, then restore him."

sentences.zh: 按前代故事，太上皇稱誥，太皇太后、皇太后曰令，今雲誥，有司誤也。

translations.literal: According to earlier dynasties' precedents, the retired emperor was styled proclamation, the retired grand empress dowager and empress dowager were styled order; now it says proclamation—the relevant offices erred.
translations.idiomatic: By precedent retired emperors used proclamation and dowagers used order; here proclamation was an error of the offices.

sentences.zh: 以宣徽南院使王峻為樞密使，右神武統軍袁鳷為宣徽南院使，陳州刺史李穀權判三司，步軍都指揮使王殷為侍衛親軍馬步都指揮使，護聖左廂都指揮使郭崇為侍衛馬軍都指揮使，奉國左廂都指揮使曹英為侍衛步軍都指揮使。

translations.literal: Wang Jun was made bureau commissioner, Yuan Ji southern palace commissioner, Chenzhou prefect Li Gu acting three departments, foot commander Wang Yin overall palace guard horse-and-foot commander, guard-for-the-sacred left commander Guo Chong guard horse commander, nation-supporting left commander Cao Ying guard foot commander.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jun became bureau commissioner, Yuan Ji southern commissioner, Li Gu acting three departments, Wang Yin guard commander, Guo Chong horse commander, Cao Ying foot commander.

sentences.zh: 鎮州、邢州馳奏，契丹寇洺州，陷內丘縣。

translations.literal: Zhenzhou and Xingzhou sent urgent memorials that the Khitan were raiding Mingzhou and had taken Neiqiu county.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenzhou and Xingzhou reported Khitan raids on Mingzhou and the fall of Neiqiu.

sentences.zh: 時契丹永康王烏裕率部族兩道入邊，內丘城小而固，契丹攻之，五日不下，敵人傷者甚眾。

translations.literal: At the time the Khitan Yongkang king Wuyu led two columns of his tribes into the borders; Neiqiu city was small but firm; the Khitan attacked five days without taking it and the enemy wounded were very many.
translations.idiomatic: Khitan prince Wuyu invaded in two columns; Neiqiu, though small, held five days and inflicted heavy Khitan losses.

sentences.zh: 時有官軍五百，在城防戍，攻急，官軍降於敵，屠其城而去。

translations.literal: At the time five hundred government troops were in the city on garrison defense; when the attack was urgent the government troops surrendered to the enemy, who slaughtered the city and left.
translations.idiomatic: Five hundred defenders surrendered under pressure; the Khitan sacked the city and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 〈（《遼史·世宗紀》：十月，自將南伐，攻下安平、內丘、束鹿等城，大獲而還。）〉

translations.literal: (From the History of Liao, Annals of Emperor Shizong: in the tenth month he personally led a southern campaign, attacked and took Anping, Neiqiu, Shulu, and other cities, and returned with great booty.)
translations.idiomatic: (From the History of Liao, Annals of Emperor Shizong: in the tenth month he campaigned south, took Anping, Neiqiu, Shulu, and others, and returned with great spoils.)

sentences.zh: 庚寅，樞密使郭威奏，左軍巡勘得飛龍使後贊款伏，與蘇逢吉、李業、閻晉卿、聶文進、郭允明等同謀，令散員都虞候奔德等下手殺害史宏肇等。

translations.literal: On day gengyin, bureau commissioner Guo Wei memorialized that the left army patrol had obtained Hou Zan's confession that he, together with Su Fengji, Li Ye, Yan Jinqing, Nie Wenjin, Guo Yunming, and others, had plotted to have the loose-duty commander Ben De and others strike and kill Shi Hongzhao.
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin Guo Wei reported Hou Zan's confession of plotting with Su Fengji, Li Ye, and others to murder Shi Hongzhao.

sentences.zh: 權開封尹劉銖具伏，朋附李業為亂，屠害將相家屬。

translations.literal: Acting Kaifeng mayor Liu Zhu confessed that he had attached himself to Li Ye in the disorder and slaughtered the families of ministers and generals.
translations.idiomatic: Acting Kaifeng mayor Liu Zhu confessed he had followed Li Ye and massacred ministers' families.

sentences.zh: 其劉銖等準誥旨處置訖，並蘇逢吉、郭允明、閻晉卿、聶文進首級，並梟於南北市，其骨肉放棄。

translations.literal: Liu Zhu and the others were disposed of according to the proclamation's order; the heads of Su Fengji, Guo Yunming, Yan Jinqing, and Nie Wenjin were all exposed in the northern and southern markets, and their flesh and bone were abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhu and the rest were executed; Su Fengji, Guo Yunming, Yan Jinqing, and Nie Wenjin's heads were displayed in both markets.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，河北諸州馳報，契丹深入。

translations.literal: On day xinmao, the Hebei prefectures sent urgent reports that the Khitan had penetrated deeply.
translations.idiomatic: On xinmao Hebei reported deep Khitan penetration.

sentences.zh: 太后誥曰：「王室多故，邊境未寧，內難雖平，外寇仍熾。

translations.literal: The dowager's proclamation stated: "The royal house has many affairs; the borders are not yet calm; internal trouble is though pacified, outer enemies still blaze.
translations.idiomatic: The dowager proclaimed: "The house has many troubles; borders are unsettled; though internal strife is over, foreign foes still rage.

sentences.zh: 據北面奏報，強敵奔沖，繼發兵師，未聞平殄，須勞上將，暫自臨戎。

translations.literal: According to northern reports, a strong enemy rushes in conflict; troops were sent in succession but no word of pacification is heard—a senior general must temporarily go to the army in person.
translations.idiomatic: Northern reports say the enemy rushes in; armies have failed— a senior general must take the field.

sentences.zh: 宜令樞密使郭威部署大軍，早謀掩擊。

translations.literal: Bureau commissioner Guo Wei should deploy the great army and early plan a concealed strike.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Wei should deploy the main force and strike quickly.

sentences.zh: 其軍國庶事，權委宰臣竇貞固、蘇禹珪、樞密使王峻等商量施行。

translations.literal: Military and civil affairs of the state are temporarily entrusted to chief ministers Dou Zhengu and Su Yugui, bureau commissioner Wang Jun, and others for deliberation and execution.
translations.idiomatic: State affairs are temporarily entrusted to Dou Zhengu, Su Yugui, Wang Jun, and others.

sentences.zh: 在京馬步兵士，委王殷都大提舉。」

translations.literal: Palace guard horse and foot soldiers in the capital were entrusted to Wang Yin's overall command."
translations.idiomatic: Capital palace horse and foot troops were placed under Wang Yin's overall command."

sentences.zh: 十二月甲午朔，郭威領大軍北征。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month, on the first day (day jiawu, new moon), Guo Wei led the great army on a northern campaign.
translations.idiomatic: At the twelfth-month new moon Guo Wei led the main army north.

sentences.zh: 丁酉，以翰林學士、尚書戶部侍郎、知制誥範質為樞密副使。

translations.literal: On day dingyou, Fan Zhi, Hanlin academician, Vice Minister of Revenue, and drafter of edicts, was made Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: On dingyou, Hanlin academician and revenue vice minister Fan Zhi became bureau vice commissioner.

sentences.zh: 〈（《東都事略》：周太祖征李守貞，每朝廷遣使賫詔，處分軍事，皆中機會，太祖問：「誰為此辭？」

translations.literal: (From the Summary of Affairs in the Eastern Capital: when the Zhou founding ancestor campaigned against Li Shouzhen, whenever the court sent envoys bearing edicts to dispose military affairs, all hit the opportune moment. The founding ancestor asked: "Who composes this language?"
translations.idiomatic: (From the Summary of Affairs in the Eastern Capital: campaigning against Li Shouzhen, Guo Wei found every court edict on military affairs perfectly timed and asked, "Who wrote them?"

sentences.zh: 使者以範質對，太祖曰：「宰相器也。」

translations.literal: The envoy answered that it was Fan Zhi. The founding ancestor said: "Material for a chief minister."
translations.idiomatic: The envoy named Fan Zhi; Guo Wei said, "Chief-minister timber."

sentences.zh: 太祖起兵入京師，遽令草太后誥及議迎湘陰公儀註。

translations.literal: When the founding ancestor raised troops and entered the capital, he urgently ordered drafting the dowager's proclamation and the protocol for welcoming the lord of Xiangyin.
translations.idiomatic: Entering the capital he ordered Fan Zhi to draft the dowager's proclamation and rites to welcome the lord of Xiangyin.

sentences.zh: 乃白太后，以質為兵部侍郎、樞密副使。）〉

translations.literal: He then reported to the dowager and made Zhi Vice Minister of War and Vice Commissioner of the Bureau.)〉
translations.idiomatic: He then had Zhi made war vice minister and bureau vice commissioner.)〉

sentences.zh: 陜州李洪信奏，馬步都指揮使聶召、奉國指揮使楊德、護聖指揮使康審澄等，與節度使判官路濤、掌書記張洞、都押衙楊紹等，同情謀叛，並殺之。

translations.literal: Shaanzhou's Li Hongxin memorialized that horse-and-foot commander Nie Zhao, nation-supporting commander Yang De, guard-for-the-sacred commander Kang Shencheng, and others, together with the commissioner's judicial officer Lu Tao, secretary Zhang Dong, chief military adjutant Yang Shao, and others, sympathized and plotted rebellion—all were killed.
translations.idiomatic: Li Hongxin reported Nie Zhao, Yang De, Kang Shencheng, and others plotting with his staff Lu Tao, Zhang Dong, and Yang Shao—all were executed.

sentences.zh: 惟康審澄夜中放火斬關，奔歸京師。

translations.literal: Only Kang Shencheng at night set fire, cut the pass, and fled back to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Only Kang Shencheng burned the gate at night and fled to the capital.

sentences.zh: 初，朝議以諸道方鎮皆是勛臣，不諳政理，其都押衙孔目官，令三司軍將內選才補之，藩帥不悅，故洪信因朝廷多故，誣奏加害焉。

translations.literal: Earlier, court deliberation held that the regional commanders in all circuits were merit ministers unfamiliar with government; their chief adjutants and clerks should be filled from talented three-departments army officers, which the military commissioners did not like; therefore Hongxin, taking advantage of the court's many troubles, falsely memorialized to harm them.
translations.idiomatic: The court had wanted to replace merit-commanders' staff with three-departments talent; the commanders resented it, and Hongxin used the crisis to frame them.

sentences.zh: 壬寅，湖南上言，朗州馬希萼引五谿蠻及淮南洪州軍來攻當道，望量差兵士於淮境牽引。

translations.literal: On day renyin, Hunan memorialized that Ma Xie of Langzhou had led Five-Divine-Man barbarians and Huainan Hongzhou troops to attack that circuit, hoping troops might be sent in some measure to the Huainan border to pull them away.
translations.idiomatic: Hunan reported Ma Xie of Langzhou attacking with Five-Divine-Man tribes and Hongzhou troops and asked for troops on the Huainan border to distract them.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，遣前淄州刺史陳恩讓領軍入淮南界，以便宜進取。

translations.literal: On day yisi, former Zizhou prefect Chen Enrang was sent to lead troops into Huainan territory to advance as opportunity allowed.
translations.idiomatic: On yisi former Zizhou prefect Chen Enrang entered Huainan with orders to act as circumstances allowed.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，遣宰相蘇禹珪及朝臣十員，往宋州迎奉嗣君。

translations.literal: On day xinhai, chief minister Su Yugui and ten court officials were sent to Songzhou to welcome the successor ruler.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai chief minister Su Yugui and ten officials went to Songzhou to welcome the heir.

sentences.zh: 壬子，樞密使郭威次澶州，何福進已下及諸軍將士，扶擁威請為天子，即日南還。

translations.literal: On day renzi, bureau commissioner Guo Wei halted at Chunzhou; He Fujin and those below and all military commanders supported and urged Wei to become Son of Heaven, and that day returned south.
translations.idiomatic: On renzi Guo Wei stopped at Chunzhou; He Fujin and the commanders forced him to become emperor and turned south the same day.

sentences.zh: 威上章於太后，言為諸軍所迫班師。

translations.literal: Wei submitted a memorial to the dowager saying he was compelled by the armies to withdraw the campaign.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Wei memorialized the dowager that the armies had forced his return.

sentences.zh: 庚申，威至北郊，駐軍於臯門村。

translations.literal: On day gengshen, Wei reached the northern suburb and encamped at Gaomen village.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen he reached the northern suburb and camped at Gaomen village.

sentences.zh: 許州巡檢、前申州刺史馬鐸奏，節度使劉信自殺。

translations.literal: Xuzhou inspector, former Shenzhou prefect Ma Duo, memorialized that commissioner Liu Xin had killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: Xuzhou inspector Ma Duo reported commissioner Liu Xin had committed suicide.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，奉太后誥，命樞密使侍中郭威監國，中外庶事，並取監國處分。

translations.literal: On day renxu, following the dowager's proclamation, bureau commissioner and Vice Grand Councilor Guo Wei was ordered to supervise the state; civil and military affairs within and without were all taken at the supervisor's disposal.
translations.idiomatic: On renxu the dowager ordered vice grand councilor Guo Wei to supervise the state with full civil and military authority.

sentences.zh: 先是，樞密使王峻以湘陰公已在宋州，慮聞澶州之事，左右變生，遣侍衛馬軍指揮使郭崇率七百騎往衛之。

translations.literal: Earlier, bureau commissioner Wang Jun, because the lord of Xiangyin was already at Songzhou, feared that on hearing of the Chunzhou affair trouble would arise at his side, and sent guard horse commander Guo Chong with seven hundred riders to guard him.
