translations.idiomatic: Earlier Wang Jun, fearing trouble when the lord of Xiangyin heard of Chunzhou, sent Guo Chong with seven hundred cavalry to guard him.

sentences.zh: 〈（《東都事略·郭崇傳》：王峻遣崇率七百騎拒瑽，遇於睢陽，崇曰：「澶州兵變，遣崇來衛乘輿，非有他也。」

translations.literal: (From the biography of Guo Chong in the Summary of Affairs in the Eastern Capital: Wang Jun sent Chong with seven hundred riders to resist Yun; they met at Suiyang. Chong said: "There was mutiny at Chanzhou; Chong was sent to guard the imperial carriage—there is no other intent."
translations.idiomatic: (From the Summary of Affairs in the Eastern Capital, biography of Guo Chong: Jun sent Chong with seven hundred riders to meet Yun at Suiyang. Chong said, "The Chanzhou troops mutinied; I came only to guard the imperial carriage—there is no other intent."

sentences.zh: 具言軍情有屬，天命已定，瑽執崇手而泣，崇即送瑽就館。）〉

translations.literal: He fully explained that army sentiment had its object and the mandate of Heaven was fixed; Yun grasped Chong's hand and wept; Chong immediately escorted Yun to his lodging.)〉
translations.idiomatic: He said the army's will was settled and Heaven's mandate fixed; Yun wept, grasped his hand, and Chong escorted him to his quarters.)〉

sentences.zh: 己未，太后誥曰：「比者，樞密使郭威，誌安社稷，議立長君，以徐州節度使赟，高祖近親，立為漢嗣，爰自藩鎮，征赴京師。

translations.literal: On day jiwei, the dowager's proclamation stated: "Recently bureau commissioner Guo Wei, intending to settle the altars, deliberated establishing a senior ruler; Xuzhou commissioner Yun, a close kinsman of Gaozu, was established as Han successor; from his post he was summoned to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: On jiwei the dowager proclaimed: "Recently Guo Wei, intending to settle the altars, deliberated establishing a senior ruler; Xuzhou commissioner Yun, Gaozu's close kinsman, was established as Han successor and summoned from his post to the capital.

sentences.zh: 雖誥命尋行，而軍情不附，天道在北，人心靡東，適當改卜之初，俾膺分土之命。

translations.literal: Although the proclamation order was soon issued, army sentiment did not attach; the Way of Heaven was in the north, human hearts did not turn east; just as the divination for change began, he was made to receive the mandate of enfeoffment.
translations.idiomatic: Though the edict went out, the armies would not follow; Heaven favored the north, not the east; at the change of fortune he received a new mandate.

sentences.zh: 赟可降授開府儀同三司、檢校太師、上柱國，封湘陰公，食邑三千戶，食實封五百戶。」

translations.literal: Yun may be demoted and appointed Acting Grand Master of the Palace, Grand Preceptor with inspection, Pillar of State, enfeoffed as Duke of Xiangyin with three thousand households' revenue and five hundred households' actual seal.
translations.idiomatic: Yun was demoted to acting grand master of the palace, inspecting grand preceptor, pillar of state, duke of Xiangyin with three thousand households and five hundred seal."

sentences.zh: 明年正月丁卯，太后誥，奉符寶於監國，可即皇帝位。

translations.literal: In the first month of the next year, on day dingmao, the dowager's proclamation delivered the talismans and treasures to the supervisor of state, who might immediately take the imperial throne.
translations.idiomatic: Next year's first month, dingmao, the dowager delivered the regalia to the regent to take the throne.

sentences.zh: 周太祖踐阼，奉太后為母，遷於西宮，上尊號曰昭聖太后。

translations.literal: When the Zhou founding ancestor ascended the throne, he honored the dowager as mother, moved her to the western palace, and gave the exalted title Zhaosheng Empress Dowager.
translations.idiomatic: When Guo Wei took the throne he honored the dowager as mother, moved her to the western palace, and titled her Zhaosheng Empress Dowager.

sentences.zh: 是月十五日，周太祖與百僚詣帝殯宮，成服親奠，不視朝七日。

translations.literal: On the fifteenth day of that month the Zhou founding ancestor with the hundred officials went to the emperor's mourning hall, completed mourning garments, and personally offered sacrifice; he did not hold court for seven days.
translations.idiomatic: On the fifteenth the Zhou founder and officials went to the late emperor's hall, mourned in person, and suspended court seven days.

sentences.zh: 又詔太常定謚曰「隱」。

translations.literal: Another edict ordered the director of sacrifices to fix the posthumous title as "Yin."
translations.idiomatic: An edict fixed his posthumous title as "Yin."

sentences.zh: 以其年八月二日，復遣前宗正卿劉皞護靈盾，備儀仗，葬於許州陽翟縣之潁陵，祔神主於高祖之寢宮。

translations.literal: On the second day of the eighth month of that year, former director of the imperial clan Liu Hao was again sent to escort the spirit shield, with full ceremonial guard burying him at Ying tomb in Yangdi county, Xuzhou; the spirit tablet was attached in Gaozu's sleeping palace.
translations.idiomatic: On the second of the eighth month Liu Hao escorted the coffin with full rites to Ying tomb in Yangdi, Xuzhou, and placed the tablet in Gaozu's shrine.

sentences.zh: 帝姿貌白晰，眉目疏朗，未即位時，目多閃掣，唾洟不止，即位之始，遽無此態，及內難將作，復如故。

translations.literal: The emperor's bearing was fair-skinned; eyebrows and eyes sparse and clear. Before he took the throne his eyes often flickered and he could not stop spitting; at the beginning of his reign this manner suddenly ceased; when internal trouble was about to arise it returned as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was fair-skinned with clear, sparse brows and eyes; before reigning his eyes twitched and he spat constantly—at his accession this stopped, but it returned when the palace coup neared.

sentences.zh: 帝自關西平定之後，稍自驕易，然畏憚大臣，未至縱恣。

translations.literal: After the pacification of the pass west, the emperor gradually became somewhat proud and easy, yet he still feared the great ministers and did not reach unrestrained license.
translations.idiomatic: After the northwest was pacified he grew somewhat arrogant but still feared his senior ministers and did not run wild.

sentences.zh: 嘗因乾象差忒，宮中或有怪異，召司天監趙延乂訊其休咎，延乂對以修德即無患，既退，遣中使就問延乂曰：「何者為德？」

translations.literal: Once because celestial signs were irregular or there were strange things in the palace, he summoned director of astronomy Zhao Yanyi to inquire of fortune and misfortune; Yanyi answered that cultivating virtue would remove worry. After he withdrew, the emperor sent a palace envoy to ask Yanyi: "What counts as virtue?"
translations.idiomatic: Once, troubled by omens or palace omens, he asked astronomer Zhao Yanyi about fortune; Yanyi said cultivate virtue. The emperor then asked, "What is virtue?"

sentences.zh: 延乂勸讀《貞觀政要》。

translations.literal: Yanyi urged reading the Essentials of Government from the Zhenguan Reign.
translations.idiomatic: Yanyi urged him to read the Essentials of Government from the Zhenguan Reign.

sentences.zh: 邇後與聶文進、郭允明、後贊狎習，信其邪說，以至於敗。

translations.literal: Later he became intimate with Nie Wenjin, Guo Yunming, and Hou Zan, trusted their wicked words, and thereby reached ruin.
translations.idiomatic: Later he grew close to Nie Wenjin, Guo Yunming, and Hou Zan, trusted their evil counsel, and was ruined.

sentences.zh: 高祖之征鄴城也，一日，帝語太祖曰：「我夜來夢爾為驢，負我升天，既舍爾，俄變為龍，舍我南去，是何祥也？」

translations.literal: When Gaozu was campaigning at Yedu, one day the emperor said to the founding ancestor: "Last night I dreamed you were a donkey carrying me up to Heaven; after setting you down you suddenly became a dragon, left me, and went south—what omen is this?"
translations.idiomatic: During Gaozu's Yedu campaign the emperor told Guo Wei, "I dreamed you were a donkey carrying me to Heaven, then a dragon that left me south—what omen is that?"

sentences.zh: 周太祖撫掌而笑。

translations.literal: The Zhou founding ancestor clapped his hands and laughed.
translations.idiomatic: Guo Wei clapped and laughed.

sentences.zh: 冥符蚃，豈偶然哉！

translations.literal: Hidden mandate thick with blessing—how could it be accidental!
translations.idiomatic: Heaven's hidden mandate—hardly accidental!

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：隱帝以尚幼之年，嗣新造之業。

translations.literal: The historiographer says: Emperor Yin, at a still tender age, succeeded a newly made enterprise.
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: Emperor Yin took a newly founded realm while still very young.

sentences.zh: 受命之主，德非禹、湯；

translations.literal: The ruler who received the mandate—his virtue was not that of Yu or Tang;
translations.idiomatic: The ruler who received the mandate lacked the virtue of Yu or Tang;

sentences.zh: 輔政之臣，復非伊、呂。

translations.literal: the ministers who assisted government were again not Yi or Lü.
translations.idiomatic: and his ministers were no Yi or Lü.

sentences.zh: 將欲保延洪之運，守不拔之基，固不可得也。

translations.literal: To wish to preserve a perpetually grand fortune and guard an unshakable foundation was impossible to obtain.
translations.idiomatic: To wish to preserve lasting fortune and an unshakable foundation was impossible.

sentences.zh: 然西摧三叛，雖僅滅於欃槍，而內稔群兇，俄自取於狼狽。

translations.literal: Yet though he in the west crushed the three rebellions and barely extinguished them at the comet's banner, within he ripened a pack of villains and soon took ruin in wolfish disarray.
translations.idiomatic: He crushed the three western rebellions yet nurtured palace villains and fell to their treachery.

sentences.zh: 自古覆宗絕祀之速者，未有如帝之甚也。

translations.literal: From antiquity, none who overturned the clan and cut off sacrifice were as swift as this emperor.
translations.idiomatic: No house in history fell faster than his.

sentences.zh: 噫！

translations.literal: Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Alas!

sentences.zh: 蓋人謀之弗臧，非天命之遽奪也。

translations.literal: It was that human plans were not good—not that Heaven's mandate was suddenly snatched away.
translations.idiomatic: It was bad human counsel, not Heaven suddenly withdrawing the mandate.
